MC/LHB/Brake dated 27.09.2018 3) RDSO letter no. MC/LHB/Brake dt. 15.04.2019 RDSO vide letters at Ref (1) and (2) above had investigated wheel shelling in LHB coaches and issued recommendations to Zonal Railways / PUs to reduce wheel shelling. Consolidated instructions for addressing the problem of Wheel Shelling in LHB Coaches were also issued to Zonal Railways / PUs vide Ref (3). Improper / Loose electrical connections of WSP system have been identified as one of the major causes of wheel shelling.

title: RDSO: Ensuring Integrity of Electrical Connections of WSP System (intermittent short-circuit / broken-cable faults)
section: Ensuring Integrity of electrical connections of WSP System
text: Improper / Loose electrical connections of WSP system have been identified as one of the major causes of wheel shelling. In this connection, extract of para 2.3.1 at Ref(1) [Carriage Research Report RDSO/CG/CRR-18001 dated 28.03.2018] is reproduced below: | | | | :--- | :--- | | 2.3.1a | A one-time drive needs to be carried out in coaching depots to ensure vibration resistant electrically tight connections in the WSP wiring system. | | 2.3.1b | Enquiries at several coaching depots bring out that the WSP wiring attention is carried out only by OEM under AMC. A feedback system needs to be formalized in maintenance depots whereby the SSE / JE in-charge of maintenance ensures that faults logged by the WSP processor of M/s FTIL and the fault counter readings for the WSP processor of M/s KBIL are acted upon and do not repeat in the next trip. The present practice of noting only the fault code of 95/99 in the WSP processor display (for eg. as brought out in Annexure A) is inadequate as these codes are displayed even when intermittent faults occur and are subsequently cleared, such as due to loose wiring. |

title: RDSO: Ensuring Integrity of Electrical Connections of WSP System (intermittent short-circuit / broken-cable faults)
section: RDSO: Ensuring Integrity of Electrical Connections of WSP System (intermittent short-circuit / broken-cable faults)
text: Ensuring integrity of Electrical connections of WSP system was also reiterated in RDSO letters at Ref (2) and (3). It is noted from the WSP fault / event data downloaded by Zonal Railways that several faults indicating short circuit / broken cable are repeatedly being set and cleared in the error logs. These intermittent faults arise mainly due to loose / damaged electrical connections in the WSP system. In many cases, the same faults are repeating in subsequent journeys even after maintenance. As such, Zonal Railways may ensure that: 1. Proper troubleshooting is carried out to arrive at the root cause of the recorded fault and any loose / damaged electrical connections are identified and attended to. It may be ensured that the same faults do not repeat after maintenance. 2. A one-time drive may be carried out in coaching depots to ensure vibration resistant electrically tight connections in the WSP wiring system. (Samir Lohani) Executive Director (Stds.)/Carriage Copy to: EDME (Chg.)/Rail Bhawan, Railway Board New Delhi- 110 001 for kind information please.

Ltd. Corporate office, Belapur Bhawan, Nawi, Mumbai-400 614 | Sub: Wheel Shelling - Wrong electrical connections in WSP system of LHB Coaches. During the recent 19th CMG, it was come to notice of RDSO that in the new LHB Coaches turned out from PUs, WSP system was automatically going in Sleep Mode after 15-20 minutes of system ON and Wheel Shelling within two-three months since their commissioning in ZRs. The problem was examined in detail with OEMs and it is learnt that these coaches were found with wrong electrical connections (at the WAGO end & in Junction Boxes at coach under frame) in Wheel Slide Protection system.

title: RDSO: Wheel Shelling — Wrong Electrical Connections in WSP System of LHB Coaches (sleep mode after 15–20 min; wiring diagrams Annexure A–F)
section: Wheel Shelling - Wrong electrical connections in WSP system of LHB Coaches
text: In connection to this, please find enclosed the electrical wiring scheme of WSP system (with exiting & modified arrangement) of LHB brake system suppliers (for the respective OEMs brake systems of LHB Coaches) for taking following action in order to ensure 100% effective working of WSP system to tackle Wheel Shelling problem: PUs: To ensure that all new LHB to be turned out with the aforesaid enclosed respective wiring scheme. ZRs: Checking & ensuring wiring connections during shop schedules (SS-1, SS-2 & SS-3) of LHB Coaches on 100% basis and depots for LHB coaches having problem of WSP going in automatic sleeping mode or suffering with Wheel Shelling. This is for kind information and necessary action please. DA: A/a. title: RDSO to PUs: Configuring of CB-12 Card in Knorr-Bremse (KBI) make WSP — required for error/event data logging
section: Configuring of CB-12 card in M/s KBI make Wheel Slide Protection (WSP)
text: भारत सरकार - रेल मंत्रालय Government of India - Ministry of Railways अनुसंधान अभिकल्प और मानक संगठन Research Designs & Standards Organisation लखनऊ - 226 011 Lucknow - 226 011 EPBX (0522) 2451200 DID (0522) 2450115 Fax (0522) 2458500 DID (0522) 2465310 No. MC/LHB/Brake Date: 03.05.2024 PCME, Integral Coach Factory Chennai, PCME, Rail Coach Factory Kapurthala, PCME, Modern Coach Factory Raebareli, Sub: Configuring of CB-12 card in M/s KBI make Wheel Slide Protection (WSP). In technical seminars held at Secunderabad and Guwahati it was reported that some of the new coaches received in coaching depots are found without configuring of the CB-12 card in M/s KBI Wheel Slide Protection (WSP) system, which results in error/event data not being logged. In this regard it is requested that the configuring of CB-12 card must be ensured by all Production Units at the time of installation of the system. Accordingly, a specific check sheet must be added in WSP test of coaches in PU for ensuring proper configuration of WSP of all makes as per OEM instructions. DA: Nil (Anil Kumar Singh) ED/Standard/Carriage Scanned with OKEN Scanner

Ref: (i) This office letter no. MC/LHB/Brake dated 27.02.2019 & 08.05.2024. (ii) Item 11 & 12 of MOM of Technical seminar held at Guwahati on 29.04.2024. Vide letter at reference above dated 27.02.2019, RDSO had issued an indicative modified drawing of Junction Box i.e. CG-19005, Alt.1 for implementation to overcome the problem of loosening of connections and water ingress in junction box. It has been observed that installation method of Junction box & speed sensor cable etc. are not uniform among PUs and also in the workshops where wiring modifications are being carried out.

title: RDSO: Standardised Installation of WSP Junction Box & Speed Sensor in LHB Coaches (installation method, cable routing)
section: Standardised Installation of WSP Junction box & Sensor in LHB Coaches
text: are not uniform among PUs and also in the workshops where wiring modifications are being carried out. Modified junction box is IP 67 compliant and is provided with installation screw holes, where MCF & RCF and many workshops are getting junction box punctured in the middle with additional holes forfeiting the IP 67 properties which is not permissible at all. In view of the above a standardized fixing arrangement and orientation of WSP wiring connectors in Junction box has been developed and to be as per following: (i) For uniform installation practice and better service life, layout of speed sensor cable and Junction box mounting on under frame is being standardized. The cable layout of speed sensor will be as per ICF drawing no.-ICF/SK3-3-5-046. (ii) The mounting bracket from under frame for junction box to be as per ICF drawing no. AAD11918 and AAA11835. (iii) The orientation of the Junction Box is being standardized and the modified drawing no.- CG-19005, Alt.2 of junction box (copy enclosed) has already been issued.

title: RDSO: Standardised Installation of WSP Junction Box & Speed Sensor in LHB Coaches (installation method, cable routing)
section: Standardised Installation of WSP Junction box & Sensor in LHB Coaches
text: Junction Box should be installed in such a way that the connecting port of speed sensor cable should be on top of the Junction Box & connecting port to Dump Valve and WSP panel should be on vertical face towards inside the coach as indicated in the drawing. Accordingly, PUs and Railways are requested to follow above standardised installation drawings of WSP Junction box & Sensor cable fitment in LHB Coaches This should be implemented with immediate effect. DA: As above. ANIL KUMAR SINGH (Anil Kumar Singh) Executive Director/ Carriage C/- 1. EDME/Coaching, Railway Board, New Delhi: For information please.

title: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
section: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
text: No: MC/WA/Genl. Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer, Sub: CTRB failures in Vande Bharat Coaches. Ref:   This office letter No. MC/EMU/WTA dated 28.11.2018 & 29.12.2023. 1. A Hot Axle case was reported in Vande Bharat coach no MC 235383 of train no 20662 on 27.06.2025 in SWR which had led to major inconvenience to passengers as train was short terminated enroute. 2. In this regard, it is noted that two more hot axle cases have been reported in May 2025, and a number of bearings have been removed in workshops during SS1 due to the issue of grease oozing, high mounted end play (MEP), abnormal sound etc. during scheduled maintenance. 3. A detailed review meeting was held by the Railway Board on this issue on

title: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
section: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
text: preventive action is required to be taken up to prevent such repetition. 4. It is noted that some times OEMs are directly providing maintenance instructions to workshops  , which is not a sound practice for uniform implementation as same must be done after due evaluation . Therefore, all the workshop are  advised  to ensure that maintenance instructions issued only by  RDSO / PUs to be followed. 5. To prevent enroute failure of Vande Bharat CTRBs, the following preventive steps to be taken up as special drive: A. In Workshop: As the majority of bearing failure has been reported in SKF make i. bearing. Thus,  all  the SKF bearings are required to be given special attention during SS1 Schedule . List of all such coaches whose MEP was not measured during SS-I  to be prepared and advised to maintenance depot for monitoring and giving  special attention during maintenance schedules for any abnormal sound, grease oozing, temperature variation or any other abnormal observations. Workshops are currently using different tools for removal of bush during ii. SS-I for measuring MEP. Workshops should ensure early availability of tools recommended by CTRB OEMs/Medha for the removal of the bush.

title: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
section: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
text: SS-I for measuring MEP. Workshops should ensure early availability of tools recommended by CTRB OEMs/Medha for the removal of the bush. Proper securing of outer cup to be ensured during removal of bush for avoiding any damage to the CTRB . For  measuring the abnormal sound, the bearing shall be given 2 iii. complete rotations in clockwise and anticlockwise direction as the sound during this rotation may be due to dropping of the rollers. Similar rotation shall also be done before measuring the Mounted End Play (MEP). During SS-I, rotate the bearing assembly to detect any abnormal iv. condition. Check the bearing mounted end play. If end play is beyond permissible limit or if any roughness is detected while rotating the bearing, OEM must be called for joint investigation and further corrective action. ICF and RDSO should also be advised for  such cases invariably. The application of lubrication in sleeve inner id and axle journal shall be v. done as per the Annexure-23 of RDSO letter MC/TSBD dated 06.04.2024. B. In Depots/stations: List to be collected of all such coaches whose MEP was not measured i. during SS-I.

title: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
section: RDSO: CTRB Failures in Vande Bharat Coaches — Maintenance of Bearings
text: B. In Depots/stations: List to be collected of all such coaches whose MEP was not measured i. during SS-I. These coaches are to be monitored  for  giving  special attention during maintenance schedules for any abnormal sound, grease oozing, temperature variation or any other abnormal observations. At the enroute station, any sign hot bearing through HABD/ thermal ii. cameras or any sudden change in temperature or temperature difference (even if within the limit) of bearings and any abnormal sound emanating from axle box must  be intimated to primary depot promptly. (Daily). The temperature of the axle box should also be taken immediately on iii. arrival of rakes at the terminating station. (Daily) . Analysis of last 15 days Readings of Axle Box Temp to identify any iv. aberration. (even if the ranges are within the limit). Further, depots must  provide temperature sensing strips (Thermax or v. equivalent) with temperature range from 50̊ C to 100 ̊ C and 5-degree graduation  on each axle box at the earliest . Any abnormal rise in temperature reflecting on the strip need to be monitored and suspected bearing should be properly investigated for grease leakage, abnormal sound etc.

title: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: भारत सरकार - रेल मंत्रालय अनुसंधान अभिकल्प और मानक संगठन लखनऊ - 226 011 EPBX (0522) 2451200 Fax (0522) 2458500 Government of India - Ministry of Railways Research Designs & Standards Organisation Lucknow - 226 011 DID (0522) 2450115 DID (0522) 2465310 No: MC/WA/Genl Date: 17.07.2025 Through e-mail Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer, ICF Chennai Sub: SKF CTRB failures in Vande Bharat coaches Ref: RDSO letter No: MC/WA/Genl. Dated: 04.07.2025 Three hot Axle case have been reported in Vande Bharat coaches within a short span of two months. one of these incidents resulted in significant passenger inconvenience due to the train being short terminated enroute. All the affected coaches were equipped with CTRBs manufactured by M/s SKF India. 2. In addition, during the SS-1 maintenance schedule in workshops, 20 CTRBs of M/s SKF India make were prematurely removed due to multiple issues, including grease oozing, high mounted end play (MEP), abnormal noise, etc. These issues present a high potential for hot axle occurrences in the future, which is a matter of serious concern. 3.

title: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: These issues present a high potential for hot axle occurrences in the future, which is a matter of serious concern. 3. In light of these developments, the Railway Board convened review meetings on 27.06.2025 and 01.07.2025, wherein it was directed that urgent corrective and preventive measures must be undertaken to prevent recurrence of such failures. 4. Subsequently, M/s SKF India has conducted preliminary investigations on a few failed bearings and observed spalling on the outer cup raceways. The suspected root cause has been attributed to ovality in the outer cup raceway. In response, SKF has shifted from sample-based measurement to 100% measurement of ovality. However, despite ongoing investigations, no substantive corrective action has been implemented at the ground level to prevent further failures. 5. Recently, Sonipat Workshop has also reported abnormal sound in two CTRBs of SKF make during SS-1 maintenance, further highlighting the persisting issues. 6. Vide reference cited above, RDSO has already advised a series of actions to be undertaken by M/s SKF India.

title: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO: Withholding of SKF make CTRB in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: 6. Vide reference cited above, RDSO has already advised a series of actions to be undertaken by M/s SKF India. However, no appreciable effort appears to have been made by the firm, and the issues with the bearings continue without resolution. In view of the above and considering the gravity of the issue, particularly its potential impact on passenger inconvenience, operational reliability, and traffic management, it is advised to withhold procurement and further fitment of SKF make CTRBs for Vande Bharat version-2 coaches until further instructions are issued by RDSO or ICF. This office letter No. MC/WA/Genl. dated 04.07.2025. (ii). M/s SKF letter No. AE/RLY/SS/AUG25/034 dated 06.08.2025. (iii). M/s SKF letter No. AE/RLY/SS/AUG25/032 dated 01.08.2025. 1. RDSO vide letter under reference (i) it was advised to Zonal Railways to provide temperature sensing strips (Thermax or equivalent) with temperature range from 50̊ C to 100 ̊ C and 5-degree graduation on each axle box at the earliest . Any abnormal rise in temperature reflecting on the strip need to be monitored and suspected bearing should be properly investigated for grease leakage, abnormal sound etc. M/s SKF vide letter under reference (ii) informed that temperature sensing strips on axle boxes for monitoring of temperature of axle boxes are being presently used in DMRC in which thermal stickers pasted on axle boxes at 3 or 9 ‘o’ clock position.

section: RDSO Guidelines for Controlling Vande Bharat CTRB Failures
text: However as per actual available space , temperature sensing strips may be fitted at  1-2 or 10-11 ‘o’ clock position on axle box housing (control arms) in existing Vande Bharat Trains, reference image is as below: Temperature sensing strip pasted on upper control arm of VB Coach Accordingly, Railways and PUs are requested to fix the temperature sensing strips at 1-2 or 10-11 ‘o’ clock position upper control arm. 2. Zonal Railways have been asking for limit of dismounting forces when central sleeves are not getting extracted easily. In this regard data for extracting forces being observed have been collected from zonal Railways and also M/s SKF vide letter under reference (iii) recommended maximum allowable safe extracting force for central sleeve is 10 tons. Accordingly, it is advised that sleeves being extracted up to 10 tons of forces meeting other parameters may be considered healthy while sleeves being extracted with more than 10 ton force to be considered susceptible due to likely presence of  high value of interference which may cause adverse effects on bearing health and therefore such bearings should be extracted and separated from sleeve and be sent to OEMs for examination and refurbishment.

Recently, a case of temperature difference of bearings on same axle of Vande Bharat Coach No. 233941 TSTC has been reported from Western Railway in which bearings mounted on affected wheelset are of two different makes (one is M/s SKF & other one is M/s Timken). For the matching  (comparable) performance  of bearings on same axle, the bearings should be mounted/dismounted on axles in pair with same make  in future maintenance schedules  or out of maintenance . Accordingly, it is requested to dismount both the bearings from axle in cases where requires only one bearing replacement and mount another both new bearings  or refurbished  bearings of same make . 4. It is found that mounting date of bearings have not been mentioned on bearings, due to this residual life of bearings could not be calculated in field during shop schedules or otherwise. It should be also ensured that residual magnetism in the bearing should not exceed 3 Gauss/0.3mT.

title: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: No. MC/WA/Genl. Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer, Integral Coach Factory, Chennai. Sub: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 schedule in Vande Bharat coaches. Ref: (i) RDSO letter No. MC/WA/Genl. dated 17.07.2025 - Withholding SKF CTRB in Vande Bharat. (ii) RDSO letter No. MC/CTRB/Defects dated 26.9.2025 & 14.102025– Pending issues with M/s Medha regarding SKF Bearing failures. 1. There have been three cases of Hot Axle involving SKF make CTRB in the month of May and June 2025 i.e. in a short span of 2 months. More than 20 CTRBs were removed till July 2025 due to multiple issues, including grease oozing, high Mounted End Play (MEP), abnormal noise etc. These issues present a high potential for hot axle occurrences. Accordingly, RDSO vide letter under ref. (i), considering the gravity of the issue, has already advised to withhold further procurement and fitment of SKF make CTRBs for Vande Bharat version-2 coaches until further instructions are issued by RDSO or ICF. 2.

title: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: 2. Further, a number of review meetings have been held with M/s Medha and Bearing’s OEMs, wherein it was advised that urgent corrective and preventive measures must be undertaken to prevent recurrence of such failures. Vide letters under ref. (ii), M/s Medha was advised to submit a conclusive report indicating root cause of failure; and suggest improvement action required to be implemented to prevent such failures in future in consultation with Bearing’s OEMs and Bogie Designer. However, final response in this regard is still awaited from M/s Medha. 3. Moreover, it has been noted that there have been regular report of premature withdrawal of M/s SKF bearing from service due to multiple issues, including grease oozing, high Mounted End Play (MEP), abnormal noise etc. So far, a total of 45 bearings have been removed from service to prevent likely hot axle issue during service. Also, during detailed investigation in number of cases, issue of spalling has been established. 4. In view of the above, it is advised that SKF Bearings should not be refitted in SS2 Schedule.

These instructions should continue in vogue till conclusive report indicating root cause of failure of M/s SKF bearings is established and suitable corrective actions taken to prevent such failures in future. The removed SKF bearings should not be sent for refurbishment till further advice from ICF/RDSO. ICF may kindly arrange to supply requisite quantity of alternate approved make CTRBs for timely execution of this changeover during SS-2 schedules. This may please be treated as urgent.

title: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: भारत सरकार - रेल मंत्रालय अनुसंधान अभिकल्प और मानक संगठन लखनऊ - 226 011 EPBX (0522) 2451200 Fax (0522) 2458500 Government of India - Ministry of Railways Research Designs & Standards Organisation Lucknow - 226 011 DID (0522) 2450115 DID (0522) 2465310 No: MC/WA/Genl Date: 17.07.2025 Through e-mail Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer, ICF Chennai Sub: SKF CTRB failures in Vande Bharat coaches Ref: RDSO letter No: MC/WA/Genl. Dated: 04.07.2025 Three hot Axle case have been reported in Vande Bharat coaches within a short span of two months. one of these incidents resulted in significant passenger inconvenience due to the train being short terminated enroute. All the affected coaches were equipped with CTRBs manufactured by M/s SKF India. 2. In addition, during the SS-1 maintenance schedule in workshops, 20 CTRBs of M/s SKF India make were prematurely removed due to multiple issues, including grease oozing, high mounted end play (MEP), abnormal noise, etc. These issues present a high potential for hot axle occurrences in the future, which is a matter of serious concern. 3.

title: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: These issues present a high potential for hot axle occurrences in the future, which is a matter of serious concern. 3. In light of these developments, the Railway Board convened review meetings on 27.06.2025 and 01.07.2025, wherein it was directed that urgent corrective and preventive measures must be undertaken to prevent recurrence of such failures. 4. Subsequently, M/s SKF India has conducted preliminary investigations on a few failed bearings and observed spalling on the outer cup raceways. The suspected root cause has been attributed to ovality in the outer cup raceway. In response, SKF has shifted from sample-based measurement to 100% measurement of ovality. However, despite ongoing investigations, no substantive corrective action has been implemented at the ground level to prevent further failures. 5. Recently, Sonipat Workshop has also reported abnormal sound in two CTRBs of SKF make during SS-1 maintenance, further highlighting the persisting issues. 6. Vide reference cited above, RDSO has already advised a series of actions to be undertaken by M/s SKF India.

section: RDSO to ICF: Replacement of SKF make CTRBs during SS-2 Schedule in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: 6. Vide reference cited above, RDSO has already advised a series of actions to be undertaken by M/s SKF India. However, no appreciable effort appears to have been made by the firm, and the issues with the bearings continue without resolution. In view of the above and considering the gravity of the issue, particularly its potential impact on passenger inconvenience, operational reliability, and traffic management, it is advised to withhold procurement and further fitment of SKF make CTRBs for Vande Bharat version-2 coaches until further instructions are issued by RDSO or ICF. title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text: The first rake of Vande Bharat Trainset Ver 2.0 (ID no 226430) was commissioned on 30th September’2022 at coaching depot MMCT for operation of train no 20901/02 (MMCT-GNC Vande Bharat Express & back). The rake was booked for SS-I on 03.04.2024 to Carriage Repair Workshop, Matunga, Central Railway & SS-I was carried out from 11.04.2024 to

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text: Vide letters dated 6.6.24 & 16.6.24, WR reported unusual vibrations in coach no 226439/C12/TC (having significant vibrations) and in other 6 coaches i.e. C-14, E1, E2, C6, C10 & C8 (having noticeable vibrations). It was also reported that passengers felt discomfort due to vibrations during journey, whenever speed crossed 110-115 kmph, leading to Rail- Madad complaints and many verbal complaints for vibrations in coach number C-12, E1, E2 & C8. WR also informed that replacement of Bogies (Make of M/s MEDHA) had been carried out in C-12 coach at slickline on 05.06.2024 as higher vibrations were observed in the coach. After replacement of bogies as detailed below, vibrations had been eliminated. Old Bogie details: North end trolley no.100004, Date of mfg. - 12/2023, South end trolley no. 100002, Date of mfg. of both trollies 06/2022. New Bogie details: North end trolley no. S-1007, Date of mfg. - 12/2023 and south end trolley no. S-1006, Date of mfg. - 12/2023.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: A. RDSO officials visited MMCT depot from 25.06.2024 to 26.06.2024. Vibrations perception & measurements were done in the train on 25.06.2024 from Mumbai Central to Ahmedabad & back. During the travel, high levels of vibrations were perceived in E2, E1, C14, C6 & C8 coaches. Perception was corroborated by recorded OMS data as well. It was also noticed that perceived vibration levels were more at center of these coaches than vibrations above bogie centers. As vibrations were accentuating at approx. 126-130 kmph in these coaches, it was suspected that these vibrations were due to wheel imbalances/wheel runouts as these coaches were having diameters of wheels from 918-930 mm & at 130 kmph, wheel rotation frequencies were approximately matching with 3rd eigen mode of carbody (12.5Hz) & were also reaching near to frequencies of primary suspended mass. It was also noted that riding of C12 coach, which had been provided with new bogies having new wheelsets, was smooth. Further, C1, C2 & C3 coaches were also having smooth ride. It may be noted that C1, C2 & C3 coaches were provided with new wheelsets during SS-I at Matunga/CR.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: It may be noted that C1, C2 & C3 coaches were provided with new wheelsets during SS-I at Matunga/CR. These observations indicated that coaches having new wheelsets were having smoother ride in comparison to coaches having wheels which were re-profiled on Surface Wheel Lathe at Matunga/CR. Accordingly, on 26-06-2024, the rake was thoroughly investigated and removed bogie from TC Coach No. 226439 (C12) was disassembled & examined by RDSO team. It was decided that all 04 wheels of TC Coach No. 226439 (C-12) should be sent to Lower Parel workshop, WR for thorough examination along with recording of following parameters for each of the wheels in as received condition & after re-profiling: - 1. Wheel Diameter & diameter difference on same axle                  2. Flange Thickness 3. Condition of wheel tread profile    4. Wheel gauge   5. Radial run out of both wheel discs of wheelsets       6. Bearing Lateral play   7. Axial run-out of both wheel discs of wheelset   8. Imbalance on each wheel disc of wheelset 9. Eccentricity of axle end holes on axle end faces on both sides for centering of wheel set during wheel profiling on surface wheel lathe. 10.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: Eccentricity of axle end holes on axle end faces on both sides for centering of wheel set during wheel profiling on surface wheel lathe. 10. Back face of flange to abutment face difference between C & C1. Annexure-I with analysis of recorded OMS data is enclosed. B. RDSO official visited Lower Parel Workshop/WR on 04.07.2024 for joint inspection of abovementioned wheelsets of old bogies removed from C12 coach. During joint inspection, wheel imbalances and run outs were noticed. Moreover, it was also noticed that centering holes on axle end faces were at 600 instead of 900, as specified in drawings and wheel re-profiling was done on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers. Annexure-II having joint report & details of wheel parameters is enclosed. C. As OMS equipment had low pass filter of 10 Hz frequency and vibrations were suspected due wheels rotating at approx 12.5 Hz with runouts/imbalances, data collection was again done by RDSO officials on 05.07.2024 with measuring equipment having wider frequency range upto 100 Hz for confirmation of vibration source.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: Data collected clearly shown unusual acceleration/energy peaks at wheel rotation frequency (approx 12.4 Hz) in the coaches (C6, E2, E1, C8 & C14) in which vibrations were being perceived & wheels of which having 600 centering holes on axle end faces were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers. Moreover, centers of these coaches were having higher vibration levels in comparison to vibrations levels just above bogie centers, indicating carbody was experiencing resonance (frequency coupling) at 130 kmph as explained above. Whereas, coaches (C1, C2 & C12) having new wheelsets/bogies did not have such unusual acceleration/energy peaks at wheel rotation frequency (approx 12.4 Hz). It may be appreciated with frequency domain analysis-DFT (Discreet Fourier Transformation) of vertical accelerations enclosed as Annexure-III. Note: All parameters were recorded on floor level inside coaches.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text:  Scenarios of fitment of 600 & 900 centers of surface wheel lathes with 600 & 900 centering holes on axle end faces were simulated by 3D model engagement. Brief is enclosed Annexure-IV. It may be appreciated that wrong centers on surface wheel lathe will result in line contact instead of surface contact, which would result in vibrations during machining, resulting in run-outs.  Western Railway was advised by RDSO on 05.07.2024 to replace the wheelsets, which were having 600 centering holes on axle end faces & were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers at Matunga Workshop, with new wheelsets at the earliest. Priority of new wheelsets was to be given to coaches having more vibrations. Moreover, it was also advised that wheelsets of other coaches, which were having 600 centering holes on axle end faces & were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers, for which wheel replacement might take time, should be planned for re- profiling on underfloor wheel lathe. ICF was also advised for provision of bogie-wise and coach-wise traceability of axles with 600 axle end centering holes and axles with 900 axle end centering holes.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text:  It was also advised to WR that removed wheelsets from coaches having vibrations & 60° axle end centring holes on axle end faces should be re-profiled on surface wheel lathe with 60° centre tool to properly maintain axial & radial runouts & dynamically balanced before reuse. Accordingly, removed wheelsets of C12 were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe with 60° center tool & dynamically balanced for reuse in C9/TC coach.  All Zonal Railways were also advised that during SSl of further Vande Bharat coaches, wheel sets shall be re-profiled on under floor wheel lathe only.  Acoordingly, Western Railway took following corrective action:  C4/MC, C5/MC, C7/MC, C11/MC & C13/MC- Wheel re-profiling on pit wheel lathe.  C9/TC- Overhauled bogie with reprofiled & balanced wheels removed from C12.  C8/MC- Bogies replaced (received from ICF).  C14/DTC-Bogies replaced (received from ICF)  C10/MC- Bogies replaced (received from ICF)  C6/TC- Bogies replaced (received from ICF)  E1/NDTC- Overhauled bogie with new wheelsets.  E2/NDTC-Bogies replaced (received from ICF) It’s to be noted here C1, C2, C3 & C12 already had new bogie or wheelsets.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text:  After above corrective actions, a trial run of the rake was again conducted from Virar to Surat & back on 21.7.24 with RDSO team onboard for vibration perception & data collection. During trial run, no vibration noticed in any of the coaches except in MMCT end of C9 coach. However, vibrations in C9 Coach on 21.7.24 were less than the level of vibrations experienced in other vibrating coaches during run on 5.7.24.  It may be noted that no unusual acceleration/energy peak was observed at wheel rotation frequency (approx. 12.4 Hz) in any coach except C9, which validated corrective actions taken. Comparatives of DFT (Discreet Fourier Transformation) of vertical accelerations & PSD (Power Spectral Density) values of vertical accelerations recorded on 5.7.24 & 21.7.24 are enclosed as Annexure V & Annexure VI, respectively. These clearly show no unusual acceleration/energy peak at wheel rotation frequency (approx. 12.4 Hz) in any coach except C9. Minor peaks were also present in C1 coach, which might be due to some wheel defect.  Further, at arrival at Virar, C9 coach was examined at Virar Car Shed.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text:  Further, at arrival at Virar, C9 coach was examined at Virar Car Shed. During Examination, it was noticed that balancing weights were available only on 05 wheels. In remaining 03 wheels, balancing weights provided by Lower Parel Workshop were not found. Details are as under: Balancing weights were not found at wheel no. 1, 6 and 8 & MMCT end of the coach was perceived & observed to have more vibration content. It may be noted here that M/s Medha (M/s SMH) & ICF conduct wheel balancing by weight removal method. For C9 coach, WR was advised telephonically to fit removed wheels of C9 again in the coach & reprofile all wheelsets of the coach on underfloor wheel lathe. After the exercise, vibrations were resolved in the coach. Though vibrations were not experienced in C1 coach, WR was advised for re-profiling of C1 coach as well on pit wheel lathe. The same has been complied by WR.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: A. Specific attentions to the issue: -
text:  During SSl of further Vande Bharat coaches, wheel sets should be re-profiled on under floor wheel lathe only.  If reprofiling is needed to be done on surface wheel lathe, followings must be ensured-  Proper fixture for motor coach wheel should be available.  Center (600 or 900) on axle end face must be checked & recorded for each wheelset & matching center on surface wheel lathe should be ensured before starting re-profiling operation.  Alignment of dead centers & degree of dead centers on both sides of surface wheel lathe must be checked, ensured & recorded before starting of every shift.  Axial & radial runouts are to be measured & recorded for each wheel after reprofiling on surface wheel lathe. Radial runout & axial runout of each wheel should be less than 0.3 mm & 0.5 mm, respectively. Above protocol can further be detailed & adopted for machining of all types of wheelsets for coaches.  ICF to circulate bogie-wise and coach-wise traceability of axles with 600 axle end centering holes and axles with 900 axle end centering holes in Vande Bharat coaches to all Zonal Railways.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
section: A. Specific attentions to the issue: -
text:  Wheels, which have already reprofiled on wrong center on surface wheel lathe & have been removed from coaches, should be re-profiled again with right center on surface wheel lathe before reuse in coaches. Axial & radial runouts are to be ensured within limit as detailed above.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text:  As Vande Bharat coaches are operated at 130 kmph, proper balancing is crucial. Followings to be ensured & recorded while assembly of wheelset-  Static balancing by proper placement of imbalances in wheel disc & brake disc.  Runouts of wheel discs, brake discs & gear boxes are to be within permissible limits as per EN 13260.  Proper dynamic balancing, preferably by material removal process. Dynamic balancing on each wheel disc plane as well as on wheelset level.  Excessive balancing should not be targeted. Balancing should be done by minimum possible material removal or minimum possible weight addition to ensure the balancing requirement of 75 gram-meter at wheelset level (addition of wheel imbalance on each wheel disc plane). Detailed instructions should be issued by ICF in consultation with M/s SMH & RDSO for balancing of wheelsets at wheelset assembly stage, covering above aspects. The same may be adopted for LHB coach wheelsets as well.  Trueness of wheel discs must be ensured during wheel disc machining on VTL before wheel assembly to ensure concentricity of bore & outer diameter of hub.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text: Quality check for the same must also be ensured at wheel disc supplier level & PU as well as workshop level.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text: Further, during onboard travel by RDSO & WR team, it was perceived by all the officials that C-6 coach was having highest level of vibration among the coaches, which may be appreciated by analysis of OMS data in Annexure-I (Comparing accelerations & ride indexes recorded for C-6 & C-12 on 25-6-24 and for C-12 on 27-5-24 on same section, i.e. VAPI-ST & ST-VAPI). Significant improvement in ride index, accelerations & vibration level is observed in C-12 on the same section after provision of new bogies. Ride qualities of E-1 & E-2 coaches have also been compared on ST-ADI section & back, analysis is enclosed as Annexure-II. The analysis in Annexure-II indicates relatively inferior riding quality in E-2. Hence, it is requested that new wheels may be provided in C-6 or E-2 coach & OMS run along with vibration perception in this coach may be repeated from Surat to MMCT in Up direction for C-6 coach or from Surat to Ahmadabad in down direction for E-2 coach for firming up the future course of action. Detailed conclusive report shall be submitted after completion of above exercise.

title: RDSO Report: Vibration in Vande Bharat Coaches after SS-1 Schedule
text: Detailed conclusive report shall be submitted after completion of above exercise. Meanwhile, attention to air suspension system leakages & snack tables as discussed with WR team may also be planned. (Shobhit Pratap Singh) Director/VDG/Carriage for Director General/Carriage

Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Vibration in Vande Bharat coaches after SS-1 schedule
text: भारत सरकार - रेल मंत्रालय Government of India - Ministry of Railways अनुसंधान अभिकल्प और मानक संगठन Research Designs & Standards Organisation लखनऊ - 226 011 Lucknow - 226 011 EPBX (0522) 2451200 DID (0522) 2450115 Fax (0522) 2458500 DID (0522) 2465310 No. MC/TS/BD Date: 25.09.2025 Principal Chief Mechanical Engineers, All Zonal Railways & PUs Sub: Vibration in Vande Bharat coaches after SS-1 schedule. Ref: (i) This office of even No. dated 05.07.2024. (ii) Report on vibration in MMCT-GNC Vande Bharat express/WR dated 31.07.2024 1. The issue of vibration in some coaches were observed after its SS1 schedule in WR in June 2024. After detailed investigation by RDSO it was revealed that axial run out, radial run out and imbalance in these wheel-sets were beyond permissible limits. Root cause for these issues was identified were due to supply of some wheel-sets having 60° axle end centring holes in initial few Vande Bharat (Ver 2.0) rakes, against of 90° axle end centring holes as specified in drawings.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Vibration in Vande Bharat coaches after SS-1 schedule
text: Re-profiling of these wheel sets having 60° axle end centring holes on surface wheel lathe having 90° centres lead to improper centring and resulted into run-outs and imbalance in such wheel sets. 2. Accordingly vide this office letter under reference (i) above, to avoid issue of use of wrong wheel centring arrangements in reprofiling during SS1 of Vande Bharat coaches in Railways, an advice was made that wheel sets shall be re-profiled on underfloor wheel lathe till further advice. 3. The above instruction was issued to avoid use of mismatched 60° and 90° axle centring with 90° centring arrangement existing in surface wheel lathe. After the above corrective action, no incidence of vibrations in Vande Bharat coaches has been reported by the Railways. Above instruction was issued for taking care of different size of centring hole on axle face. 4. Now, it is understood that all the wheel-sets are getting supplied with 90° centring holes in axles and accordingly re-profiling can also be done on surface wheel lathe during SS-1 schedule in the workshops with following precautions: i. Proper fixture for motor coach wheel should be available. ii.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Vibration in Vande Bharat coaches after SS-1 schedule
text: i. Proper fixture for motor coach wheel should be available. ii. Centre (60° or 90°) on axle end face must be checked & recorded for each wheelset & matching centre on surface wheel lathe should be ensured before starting re-profiling operation. iii. Alignment of dead centers & degree of dead centers on both sides of surface wheel lathe must be checked, ensured & recorded before starting of every shift. iv. Axial & radial runouts are to be measured & recorded for each wheel after re-profiling on surface wheel lathe. Radial runout & axial runout of each wheel should be less than 0.3 mm & 0.5 mm, respectively. Railways are requested to ensure above guidelines and close monitoring of turned out rake (after SS-1 with re-profiled wheel from surface wheel lathe) to be done for any issue of vibration. Copy of the letters at ref.(i) & (ii) are enclosed herewith for reference. This is for kind information and necessary action please. DA: As above (A.K.Singh) Executive Director Stds./Carriage CC: 1. EDME/Coaching, Railway Board 2. PED/CAMTECH, Gwalior

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: The first rake of Vande Bharat Trainset Ver 2.0 (ID no 226430) was commissioned on 30th Vande Bharat Express & back). The rake was booked for SS-I on 03.04.2024 to Carriage Repair Workshop, Matunga, Central Railway & SS-I was carried out from 11.04.2024 to Vide letters dated 6.6.24 & 16.6.24, WR reported unusual vibrations in coach no 226439/C12/TC (having significant vibrations) and in other 6 coaches i.e. C-14, E1, E2, C6, C10 & C8 (having noticeable vibrations). It was also reported that passengers felt discomfort due to vibrations during journey, whenever speed crossed 110-115 kmph, leading to Rail- Madad complaints and many verbal complaints for vibrations in coach number C-12, E1, E2 & C8. WR also informed that replacement of Bogies (Make of M/s MEDHA) had been carried out in C-12 coach at slickline on 05.06.2024 as higher vibrations were observed in the coach. After replacement of bogies as detailed below, vibrations had been eliminated. Old Bogie details: North end trolley no.100004, Date of mfg. - 12/2023, South end trolley no. 100002, Date of mfg. of both trollies 06/2022. New Bogie details: North end trolley no. S-1007, Date of mfg. - 12/2023 and south end trolley no.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: 100002, Date of mfg. of both trollies 06/2022. New Bogie details: North end trolley no. S-1007, Date of mfg. - 12/2023 and south end trolley no. S-1006, Date of mfg. - 12/2023.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: A. RDSO officials visited MMCT depot from 25.06.2024 to 26.06.2024. Vibrations perception & measurements were done in the train on 25.06.2024 from Mumbai Central to Ahmedabad & back. During the travel, high levels of vibrations were perceived in E2, E1, C14, C6 & C8 coaches. Perception was corroborated by recorded OMS data as well. It was also noticed that perceived vibration levels were more at center of these coaches than vibrations above bogie centers. As vibrations were accentuating at approx. 126-130 kmph in these coaches, it was suspected that these vibrations were due to wheel imbalances/wheel runouts as these coaches were having diameters of wheels from 918-930 mm & at 130 kmph, wheel rotation frequencies were approximately matching with 3rd eigen mode of carbody (12.5Hz) & were also reaching near to frequencies of primary suspended mass. It was also noted that riding of C12 coach, which had been provided with new bogies having new wheelsets, was smooth. Further, C1, C2 & C3 coaches were also having smooth ride. It may be noted that C1, C2 & C3 coaches were provided with new wheelsets during SS-I at Matunga/CR.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: It may be noted that C1, C2 & C3 coaches were provided with new wheelsets during SS-I at Matunga/CR. These observations indicated that coaches having new wheelsets were having smoother ride in comparison to coaches having wheels which were re-profiled on Surface Wheel Lathe at Matunga/CR. Accordingly, on 26-06-2024, the rake was thoroughly investigated and removed bogie from TC Coach No. 226439 (C12) was disassembled & examined by RDSO team. It was decided that all 04 wheels of TC Coach No. 226439 (C-12) should be sent to Lower Parel workshop, WR for thorough examination along with recording of following parameters for each of the wheels in as received condition & after re-profiling: - 1. Wheel Diameter & diameter difference on same axle                  2. Flange Thickness 3. Condition of wheel tread profile    4. Wheel gauge   5. Radial run out of both wheel discs of wheelsets       6. Bearing Lateral play   7. Axial run-out of both wheel discs of wheelset   8. Imbalance on each wheel disc of wheelset 9. Eccentricity of axle end holes on axle end faces on both sides for centering of wheel set during wheel profiling on surface wheel lathe. 10.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: Eccentricity of axle end holes on axle end faces on both sides for centering of wheel set during wheel profiling on surface wheel lathe. 10. Back face of flange to abutment face difference between C & C1. Annexure-I with analysis of recorded OMS data is enclosed. B. RDSO official visited Lower Parel Workshop/WR on 04.07.2024 for joint inspection of abovementioned wheelsets of old bogies removed from C12 coach. During joint inspection, wheel imbalances and run outs were noticed. Moreover, it was also noticed that centering holes on axle end faces were at 600 instead of 900, as specified in drawings and wheel re-profiling was done on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers. Annexure-II having joint report & details of wheel parameters is enclosed. C. As OMS equipment had low pass filter of 10 Hz frequency and vibrations were suspected due wheels rotating at approx 12.5 Hz with runouts/imbalances, data collection was again done by RDSO officials on 05.07.2024 with measuring equipment having wider frequency range upto 100 Hz for confirmation of vibration source.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: Onboard Vibration Perception & Measurements by RDSO officials:
text: Data collected clearly shown unusual acceleration/energy peaks at wheel rotation frequency (approx 12.4 Hz) in the coaches (C6, E2, E1, C8 & C14) in which vibrations were being perceived & wheels of which having 600 centering holes on axle end faces were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers. Moreover, centers of these coaches were having higher vibration levels in comparison to vibrations levels just above bogie centers, indicating carbody was experiencing resonance (frequency coupling) at 130 kmph as explained above. Whereas, coaches (C1, C2 & C12) having new wheelsets/bogies did not have such unusual acceleration/energy peaks at wheel rotation frequency (approx 12.4 Hz). It may be appreciated with frequency domain analysis-DFT (Discreet Fourier Transformation) of vertical accelerations enclosed as Annexure-III. Note: All parameters were recorded on floor level inside coaches.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: Scenarios of fitment of 600 & 900 centers of surface wheel lathes with 600 & 900 centering holes on axle end faces were simulated by 3D model engagement. Brief is enclosed Annexure-IV. It may be appreciated that wrong centers on surface wheel lathe will result in line contact instead of surface contact, which would result in vibrations during machining, resulting in run-outs. Western Railway was advised by RDSO on 05.07.2024 to replace the wheelsets, which were having 600 centering holes on axle end faces & were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers at Matunga Workshop, with new wheelsets at the earliest. Priority of new wheelsets was to be given to coaches having more vibrations. Moreover, it was also advised that wheelsets of other coaches, which were having 600 centering holes on axle end faces & were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe having 900 centers, for which wheel replacement might take time, should be planned for re- profiling on underfloor wheel lathe. ICF was also advised for provision of bogie-wise and coach-wise traceability of axles with 600 axle end centering holes and axles with 900 axle end centering holes.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: It was also advised to WR that removed wheelsets from coaches having vibrations & 60° axle end centring holes on axle end faces should be re-profiled on surface wheel lathe with 60° centre tool to properly maintain axial & radial runouts & dynamically balanced before reuse. Accordingly, removed wheelsets of C12 were re-profiled on surface wheel lathe with 60° center tool & dynamically balanced for reuse in C9/TC coach. All Zonal Railways were also advised that during SSl of further Vande Bharat coaches, wheel sets shall be re-profiled on under floor wheel lathe only. Acoordingly, Western Railway took following corrective action:

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: After above corrective actions, a trial run of the rake was again conducted from Virar to Surat & back on 21.7.24 with RDSO team onboard for vibration perception & data collection. During trial run, no vibration noticed in any of the coaches except in MMCT end of C9 coach. However, vibrations in C9 Coach on 21.7.24 were less than the level of vibrations experienced in other vibrating coaches during run on 5.7.24. It may be noted that no unusual acceleration/energy peak was observed at wheel rotation frequency (approx. 12.4 Hz) in any coach except C9, which validated corrective actions taken. Comparatives of DFT (Discreet Fourier Transformation) of vertical accelerations & PSD (Power Spectral Density) values of vertical accelerations recorded on 5.7.24 & 21.7.24 are enclosed as Annexure V & Annexure VI, respectively. These clearly show no unusual acceleration/energy peak at wheel rotation frequency (approx. 12.4 Hz) in any coach except C9. Minor peaks were also present in C1 coach, which might be due to some wheel defect. Further, at arrival at Virar, C9 coach was examined at Virar Car Shed. During Examination, it was noticed that balancing weights were available only on 05 wheels.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: During Examination, it was noticed that balancing weights were available only on 05 wheels. In remaining 03 wheels, balancing weights provided by Lower Parel Workshop were not found. Details are as under: Balancing weights were not found at wheel no. 1, 6 and 8 & MMCT end of the coach was perceived & observed to have more vibration content. It may be noted here that M/s Medha (M/s SMH) & ICF conduct wheel balancing by weight removal method. For C9 coach, WR was advised telephonically to fit removed wheels of C9 again in the coach & reprofile all wheelsets of the coach on underfloor wheel lathe. After the exercise, vibrations were resolved in the coach. Though vibrations were not experienced in C1 coach, WR was advised for re-profiling of C1 coach as well on pit wheel lathe. The same has been complied by WR.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: A. Specific attentions to the issue: -
text: During SSl of further Vande Bharat coaches, wheel sets should be re-profiled on under floor wheel lathe only. If reprofiling is needed to be done on surface wheel lathe, followings must be ensured- Proper fixture for motor coach wheel should be available. Center (600 or 900) on axle end face must be checked & recorded for each wheelset & matching center on surface wheel lathe should be ensured before starting re-profiling operation. Alignment of dead centers & degree of dead centers on both sides of surface wheel lathe must be checked, ensured & recorded before starting of every shift. Axial & radial runouts are to be measured & recorded for each wheel after reprofiling on surface wheel lathe. Radial runout & axial runout of each wheel should be less than 0.3 mm & 0.5 mm, respectively. Above protocol can further be detailed & adopted for machining of all types of wheelsets for coaches. ICF to circulate bogie-wise and coach-wise traceability of axles with 600 axle end centering holes and axles with 900 axle end centering holes in Vande Bharat coaches to all Zonal Railways.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
section: A. Specific attentions to the issue: -
text: Wheels, which have already reprofiled on wrong center on surface wheel lathe & have been removed from coaches, should be re-profiled again with right center on surface wheel lathe before reuse in coaches. Axial & radial runouts are to be ensured within limit as detailed above.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: As Vande Bharat coaches are operated at 130 kmph, proper balancing is crucial. Followings to be ensured & recorded while assembly of wheelset- Static balancing by proper placement of imbalances in wheel disc & brake disc. Runouts of wheel discs, brake discs & gear boxes are to be within permissible limits as per EN 13260. Proper dynamic balancing, preferably by material removal process. Dynamic balancing on each wheel disc plane as well as on wheelset level. Excessive balancing should not be targeted. Balancing should be done by minimum possible material removal or minimum possible weight addition to ensure the balancing requirement of 75 gram-meter at wheelset level (addition of wheel imbalance on each wheel disc plane). Detailed instructions should be issued by ICF in consultation with M/s SMH & RDSO for balancing of wheelsets at wheelset assembly stage, covering above aspects. The same may be adopted for LHB coach wheelsets as well. Trueness of wheel discs must be ensured during wheel disc machining on VTL before wheel assembly to ensure concentricity of bore & outer diameter of hub.

title: Vibration in Vande Bharat Wheels after SS-1 Schedule
text: Quality check for the same must also be ensured at wheel disc supplier level & PU as well as workshop level.

section: RDSO: Failure of Primary Coil Springs in Vande Bharat Trains
text: 15. North Western Railway, Jaipur - 302 006. 16. North Central Railway, Allahabad-211001 17. Konkan Railway Corpo. Ltd., Navi Mumbai - 400 614. Sub: Failure of primary Coil Springs in Vande Bharat Trains. 24 failure cases of primary coil springs in Vande Bharat coaches have been reported to RDSO. In most of failures of primary springs, cracks have appeared in 1st active coil i.e. at approx. 1.1-1.4 turn from end. In one case of coil spring failure, which has been reported by SCR in coach no.235012 TC of train no.20833/34 VSKP-SC on 07.01.2024, it was observed that failure/crack appeared in ineffective coil at bottom end i.e. at 0.5 turn from the end. Accordingly, RDSO official has visited VSKP depot on 12.01.2024 & conducted thorough investigation of the case. In investigation, it has been observed that bottom ineffective end of the failed coil spring was seating on projected weld leg of collar of bottom centering disc (lower spring pad with bump stop). For appreciation, photographs in Annexure-I may be pursued. Point of interaction of projected weld leg with bottom end of coil spring became stress concentration point, resulting in coil spring failure.

title: RDSO: Failure of Primary Coil Springs in Vande Bharat Trains
section: RDSO: Failure of Primary Coil Springs in Vande Bharat Trains
text: Point of interaction of projected weld leg with bottom end of coil spring became stress concentration point, resulting in coil spring failure. It is pertinent that RDSO, vide letter MC/TS/BD date 10.11.2023, has already advised M/s Medha to switchover to single piece design of bottom centering disc (lower spring pad with bump stop). In view of above, it is requested that thorough examination of bottom centering disc & top spring pad along-with damper & axle box pivot bush should also be done in case of any coil springs failure. It is also requested that all bottom centering discs (lower spring pad with bump stop) of Vande Bharat trains should be thoroughly inspected at first given opportunity at depot or workshops for identifying any manufacturing defect & further necessary action.
